V.}}</noinclude>Scribes murmured, saying to his disciples, Why doe you eate and drinke vvith Publicans and sinners? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=31}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} answering said to them, They that are vvhole, neede not the Physicion: but they that are il at ease. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=32}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ came not to call those, who presume of their owne iustice, and that coumpt them selues to haue no neede of Christ.}}∷ I came not to call the iust, but sinners to penance.⊣ {{verse|chapter=5|verse=33}}† But they said to him, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mat. 9, 14. Mar. 2, 18. Lu. 5, 33.''}}* VVhy doe the disciples of Iohn {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''See S. Mat. Annot. c. 9, 14.''}}* fast often, and make obsecrations, and of the Pharisees in like maner: but thine doe eate and drinke? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=34}}† To vvhom he said, Why, can you make the children of the bridegrome fast vvhiles the bridegrome is vvith them? {{verse|chapter=5|verse=35}}† But the daies vvil come: and vvhen the bridegrome shal be taken avvay from them, then they shal fast in those daies. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=36}}† And he said a similitude also vnto them, That no man putteth a peece from a nevv garment into an old garment: othervvise both he breaketh the nevv, and the peece from the nevv agreeth not vvith the old. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=37}}† And no bodie putteth nevv vvine into old bottels: othervvise the nevv vvine vvil breake the bottels, and it self vvil be shed, and the bottels vvil be lost. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=38}}† But nevv vvine is to be put into nevv bottels: and both are preserued together. {{verse|chapter=5|verse=39}}† And no man drinking old, vvil nevv by and by. for he saith, The old is better.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. V.}}}}

''3. One ship Simons.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters ship.}}It is purposely expressed that there were two shippes, and that one of them was Peters, and that Christ went into that one, and sate downe in it, and that sitting he taught out of that ship: no doubt to signifie the Church resembled by Peters ship, and that in it is the chaire of Christ, and only true preaching.

''6. A great multitude of fishes.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters fishing.}}Likewise by this significatiue miracle wrought about Peters fishing, is euidently forshewed vvhat wonderful successe Peter should haue in conuerting men to Christ, both Ievves and Gentiles. as vvhen at one draught, that is to say, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 2, 41. 4, 4''.}}at one Sermon he drewe into his ship, which is Christes Church, a great number of men, as he did now fishes: and so continually by him self and his Successors vnto the worlds end.

''7. Beckened to their fellowes.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters coadiutors.}}Peter had so much worke that he called for helpe and ioyned vnto him the other ship, representing to vs his Copartiners in the preaching of the Gospel, and the coniunction of the Synagogue and the people of Gentilitie vnto Peters ship, that is, to the Church of Christ. ''Ambro. li. 4. in Luc. c. vlt''.

''10. Thou shalt be taking men.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters preeminence in fishing for mens soules.}}That al this aforesaid did properly meane Peters trauailes to come, in the conuersion of the world to Christ, and his prerogatiue before al men therein, it is euident by Christs special promis made to him seuerally and apart in this place, that he should be made the taker of men. though to other he giueth also, as to Peters cooperators and coadiutors, the like office. ''Mat. 4, 19''.

''19. Went vp vpon the roofe.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Zeale of soules.}}A strange diligence in procuring corporal health of and by Christ: and an example for vs of the like or greater, to obteine saluation of him either for our selues or our frendes, and to seeke to his Church and Sacraments with what extraordinarie paine soeuer.

''20. Whose faith.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The intercession of others,}}Great is God (saith S. Ambrose) and pardoneth one sort through the merites of others. therfore if thou doubt to obtaine forgiuenesse of thy great offenses, ioyne vnto thy self intercessors, vse the Churches helpe, which may pray for thee and obtaine for thee that which our Lord might denie to thy self. ''Amb. li. 5 in Luc''.<noinclude>{{continues|''24. The''}}</noinclude>
